description: Born in the Bronx in 1973, hip-hop invented DJ, rap, breakdance and graffiti, then conquered the planet.

hero.hook: A block party in the Bronx, and a global culture was born.

blocks.text: Hip-hop is not just a musical genre. It's a culture born out of adversity, in the **Bronx** of New York in the early **1970**.

In fifty years, this movement invented by young African-Americans and Puerto Ricans has transformed music, fashion and language. Here's how a block party became the common language of the world's youth.

The context is brutal. Between 1950 and 1972, [[Robert Moses's highway policy]] crossed the neighborhood: the [[Cross-Bronx Expressway]], led by urban planner [[Robert Moses]], destroyed tens of thousands of homes. [[Real estate speculation]] even pushes some owners to burn down their buildings for insurance. We then say: “the Bronx is burning”.

**August 11, 1973**, at 1520 Sedgwick Avenue, Jamaican immigrant **Clive Campbell**, known as **Kool DJ Herc**, is organizing a party in the common room of his building. He invented the *breakbeat*: with two turntables, he isolated and extended the most danceable rhythmic part of a record. The DJ becomes a creator, not just a broadcaster.

blocks.caption: Kool Herc: two turntables, a break, and the hip-hop begins.

blocks.text: His “Herculords” system was so powerful that he sometimes illegally plugged it into street lamps.

sections.title: The Bronx in Ruins and Kool Herc's Party

blocks.text: Hip-hop is structured around four disciplines. The **DJing** is refined with **Grandmaster Flash**, which treats the turntable like an instrument. The **MCing** (Master of Ceremonies) transformed calls to the public into rhythmic poetry: this was the birth of rap.

blocks.caption: Breakdance and graffiti: the body and the wall as scenes.

blocks.text: Added to this are **breakdancing** (B-Boying), an athletic dance, and **graffiti**, which transforms metro trains into mobile galleries. **Afrika Bambaataa**, former gang member, founded the **Universal Zulu Nation** to replace violence with artistic competition: peace, love, unity, pleasure.
[[Scratching]] was born by accident in 1975: **Great Wizzard Theodore**, 12 years old, jams a record in his hand to hear his mother calling him.

sections.title: Four pillars: DJ, MC, dance, graffiti

blocks.text: In **1979**, *Rapper's Delight* from the **Sugarhill Gang** proves that rap can be a worldwide hit, even if the pioneers consider it too "studio". In **1982**, *The Message* by **Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five** imposes the social chronicle of the ghetto.

blocks.caption: Rapper's Delight (1979): rap hits the charts.

blocks.text: In the 1990s, East/West rivalry structured the industry. In New York, [[The Notorious B.I.G.]] focuses on lyrical virtuosity. In Los Angeles, **N.W.A** and [[Tupac Shakur]] developed gangsta rap, which denounced police violence. The rapper also becomes an entrepreneur: labels, clothes, brands.
The loop of *Rapper's Delight* is not a sample: it is a studio re-recording of *Good Times* by Chic, for fear of lawsuits.

sections.title: From the Bronx to the charts: the commercial explosion

blocks.text: In the 21st century, **Eminem**, **Kanye West** or **Kendrick Lamar** elevate the genre. In **2018**, Lamar won a Pulitzer Prize for music: unprecedented institutional recognition. [[Musical sampling]] has become a universal technique. France is the second largest rap market in the world.

events.detail: Kool Herc invents breakbeat in the Bronx.
events.title: Sedgwick Avenue Party

blocks.text: Born on August 11, 1973 in the Bronx with Kool Herc, hip-hop went from local outlet to the most influential culture of the contemporary era.

sections.title: A culture that has become a global language

title: Hip-hop: birth of a culture
